report.incidentSummary: On 2026-10-05 starting around 09:00 IST (03:30 UTC), users reported duplicate debits for their SIP instalments. The morning SIP debit batch ran from 00:30 UTC to 02:30 UTC. During this batch, debit-worker experienced confirmation timeouts with partner bank Kaveri, because a configuration change on 2026-10-04 had reduced debit-worker's bank confirmation timeout from 8000ms to 3000ms. When Kaveri bank's response times surged to 5000ms-8462ms, debit-worker prematurely timed out attempt 1 and submitted attempt 2 with a new debit ID. Kaveri bank processed both the late attempt 1 and attempt 2, resulting in duplicate debits for at least 105 mandates.
report.rootCauseStatement: Configuration change CHG-48217 lowered debit-worker's bank.confirm_timeout_ms from 8000ms to 3000ms on 2026-10-04. When partner bank Kaveri's API response latency rose above 3000ms (p95 reaching ~7000ms-8462ms) during the morning batch processing on 2026-10-05, debit-worker prematurely declared attempt 1 timed out and submitted attempt 2 with a new debit ID. Kaveri bank subsequently fulfilled both the late attempt 1 and attempt 2, resulting in duplicate debits from customer bank accounts.

hypotheses.cause: Config change CHG-48217 reduced debit-worker's bank confirmation timeout from 8000ms to 3000ms. When Kaveri bank responses exceeded 3000ms (5000ms-8462ms) during the morning batch, debit-worker prematurely timed out and issued attempt 2 with a new debit ID; Kaveri bank subsequently fulfilled both the late attempt 1 and attempt 2, causing duplicate debits.
hypotheses.rationale: Directly confirmed by configuration change records, debit-worker timeout and retry logs, bank-connector latency metrics and logs, and duplicate-check error logs explicitly linking late responses on attempt 1 with attempt 2 debits.

hypotheses.cause: Partner bank Kaveri experienced severe external processing latency degradation during the morning batch run, with p95 response latency jumping from under 2000ms to 7000ms-8462ms and bank timeouts spiking, causing confirmation delays that triggered resubmissions.
hypotheses.rationale: Kaveri bank did suffer elevated latency, but prior to CHG-48217 the timeout budget was 8000ms; most responses (and late attempt 1 executions) were fulfilled between 3000ms and 8000ms. The duplicate debits occurred primarily because debit-worker aborted at 3000ms and retried non-idempotently.

hypotheses.cause: Duplicate execution of the SIP debit batch job by job-scheduler, or message redelivery/lag on the message queue, triggered duplicate debits.
hypotheses.rationale: job-scheduler ran sip-debit-batch exactly once (run_c511c4c2). Message queue depth, consumer lag, and consumer group rebalances showed no duplicate messages or debits queue backlog.

hypotheses.cause: Deployment of SIP management screen v2 in mf-order-service (CHG-48225) triggered duplicate debit orders.
hypotheses.rationale: CHG-48225 deployed at 03:45 UTC (09:15 IST), well after user complaints started (~03:30 UTC / 09:00 IST) and after the batch had finished at 02:30 UTC (08:00 IST). Order logs show normal single orders.

facts.statement: On 2026-10-04 at 13:10:00 UTC (18:40 IST), configuration change CHG-48217 lowered debit-worker bank.confirm_timeout_ms from 8000ms to 3000ms.
job-scheduler triggered sip-debit-batch exactly once (run_c511c4c2) starting at 2026-10-05T00:30:00Z and completing at 2026-10-05T02:30:00Z.
Between 00:50 UTC and 02:30 UTC, debit-worker experienced an elevated retry rate specifically for bank 'kaveri', with retry_count reaching ~250/min and debit_count rising from ~730/min to ~1100/min.
debit-worker logged 2,236 instances of 'no confirmation from bank within 3000ms; resubmitting (attempt 2)' for bank kaveri between 00:50:01 UTC and 02:34:59 UTC.
bank_latency_p95_ms for Kaveri bank spiked between 00:50 UTC and 02:25 UTC to 6,987ms-8,462ms, while other partner banks remained under 4,000ms.
bank-connector logged numerous Kaveri debit response times between 3000ms and 8000ms (such as 5238ms, 5434ms, 5682ms, 5899ms, 7046ms, 7797ms).

debit-worker logged 953 occurrences of 'confirmed by bank (late response to attempt # after #ms)' and 105 duplicate-check error warnings (error_code DUPLICATE_DEBIT) for Kaveri mandates between 02:40 UTC and 03:29 UTC.
The 'debits' message-queue queue depth and consumer lag remained low and stable throughout the window, and zero message-queue error logs occurred.
Deployments during the investigation window included mandate-service at 02:16 UTC (CHG-48449) and mf-order-service at 03:45 UTC (CHG-48225).

inferences.statement: Lowering bank.confirm_timeout_ms from 8000ms to 3000ms caused debit-worker to prematurely time out in-flight Kaveri bank debit requests that were taking between 3000ms and 8000ms to process.
When attempt 1 timed out at 3000ms, debit-worker submitted attempt 2 with a new debit ID rather than maintaining an upstream idempotency presentation key recognized by Kaveri bank.
Because Kaveri bank eventually fulfilled both the delayed initial debit attempt (attempt 1) and the retry (attempt 2), both debits succeeded against the user's account, resulting in duplicate debits.
mf-order-service deployment CHG-48225 did not cause the incident because it was deployed at 03:45 UTC (09:15 IST), well after support tickets began around 03:30 UTC (09:00 IST).

assumptions.statement: Kaveri bank's presentation API does not enforce cross-request mandate instalment idempotency when presentations carry different debit IDs.

timeline.event: Configuration change CHG-48217 applied to debit-worker by m.bose, changing bank.confirm_timeout_ms from 8000ms to 3000ms.
job-scheduler starts sip-debit-batch (run_c511c4c2); debit-worker begins processing debit mandates.
Kaveri bank p95 response latency degrades past 3000ms (reaching 5000ms-8462ms); debit-worker begins logging 3000ms timeouts and dispatching attempt 2 resubmissions.
debit-worker begins logging late confirmations from Kaveri bank for attempt 1 alongside processing of attempt 2.
job-scheduler sip-debit-batch run_c511c4c2 completes successfully; Kaveri bank latency normalizes to ~2000ms.
debit-worker duplicate-check routine logs 105 instances of mandates having 2 confirmed debits for the 2026-10-05 instalment.
Support tickets begin arriving as users receive duplicate debit SMS notifications from Kaveri bank.
CHG-48225 deployed to mf-order-service (SIP management screen v2 APIs).

confidence.rationale: The config change timing, specific timeout threshold match (3000ms), bank latency records (5000ms-8462ms), retry attempt logs, and duplicate confirmation logs on debit-worker provide conclusive end-to-end evidence.

recommendedActions.action: Revert debit-worker's bank.confirm_timeout_ms from 3000ms back to 8000ms (or higher, aligned with bank-connector's provider timeout).
recommendedActions.rationale: Prevents debit-worker from aborting and retrying debit calls while partner banks are still processing the initial request within normal batch latency bounds.
recommendedActions.verification: Check debit-worker configuration key bank.confirm_timeout_ms and verify zero premature timeout warnings during the next batch run.

recommendedActions.action: Identify all affected mandate instalments from debit-worker duplicate-check logs (error_code DUPLICATE_DEBIT) and initiate automated customer refunds.
recommendedActions.rationale: Users have been debited twice for their 2026-10-05 SIP instalment.
recommendedActions.verification: Query debit-worker duplicate-check logs and bank settlement reports to ensure every double debit has a corresponding refund record.

recommendedActions.action: Implement end-to-end presentation idempotency keys at bank-connector and partner bank APIs based on mandate ID and instalment date rather than unique debit attempt IDs.
recommendedActions.rationale: Ensures partner banks deduplicate retries even if debit-worker generates a new debit ID upon retry.
recommendedActions.verification: Test partner bank API integration with mock delayed responses and verify duplicate presentation requests return existing debit confirmation rather than debiting twice.

recommendedActions.action: Enforce strict configuration validation and architectural safeguards preventing client-side timeouts in debit-worker from being set lower than downstream gateway timeouts in bank-connector.
recommendedActions.rationale: Mismatched timeouts between caller and gateway inherently cause duplicate processing on retries.
recommendedActions.verification: Add CI/CD config linting or service startup validation comparing debit-worker timeout against bank-connector gateway timeout.

findings.summary: Within the specified investigation window (2026-10-04T20:00 to 2026-10-05T04:30 UTC), changes were applied only to mandate-service (CHG-48449 at 02:16 UTC, HTTP client library upgrade) and mf-order-service (CHG-48225 at 03:45 UTC, SIP screen v2 APIs, deployed after tickets started). However, a critical configuration change CHG-48217 was applied to debit-worker at 2026-10-04T13:10 UTC reducing bank.confirm_timeout_ms from 8000ms to 3000ms. Because debit-worker retries twice upon confirmation timeout while bank-connector allows up to 8000ms for bank-apis, any debit response taking between 3s and 8s triggers duplicate debit resubmissions. Past incident PIR-2008 also caused duplicate debits, but via duplicate scheduler batch execution.

observations.statement: Within the window 2026-10-04T20:00:00Z to 2026-10-05T04:30:00Z, mandate-service was deployed at 2026-10-05T02:16:54Z (CHG-48449, HTTP client upgrade v2.3.0 -> v2.3.1) and mf-order-service was deployed at 2026-10-05T03:45:00Z (CHG-48225, SIP management screen v2 APIs v4.0.7 -> v4.1.0). No changes occurred in debit-worker, bank-connector, or job-scheduler during this window.

The mf-order-service deployment (CHG-48225) occurred at 03:45 UTC (09:15 IST), which is after user complaint tickets had already begun around 03:30 UTC (09:00 IST), ruling it out as the initial trigger for the duplicate debits.

On 2026-10-04T13:10:00Z (prior to the early morning batch run), a configuration change CHG-48217 was applied to debit-worker by m.bose, changing bank.confirm_timeout_ms from 8000ms down to 3000ms to speed up the morning batch.

In the service dependency graph, debit-worker retries up to 2 times if bank confirmation is not received within the timeout, whereas bank-connector has an 8000ms timeout with bank-apis. Reducing debit-worker timeout to 3000ms causes debit-worker to time out and resubmit debits while partner bank API calls are still executing or take longer than 3000ms.

Past incident PIR-2008 (2026-09-08 SEV1) involved SIP instalments debited twice for ~3,000 users caused by job-scheduler running sip-debit-batch twice after a leader election, which was resolved by acquiring a distributed lock. Past incident PIR-1410 (2026-08-26 SEV3) involved partner bank batch processing slowdowns. Past incident PIR-1110 (2026-08-07 SEV3) involved duplicate reminder pushes after scheduler leader election, resolved with idempotency keys.
